title: Davy Tough crossing to the South Side
summary: Jones credits Davy Tough with learning from Chicago's black musicians and showing white players what he heard.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I happened to mention that and the last few drummers I mentioned, most of them were white. I was trying to just make an analogy here, Jo. It seems as if every one of the great white bands was really steamrolled by these very great drummers we've just named. We haven't talked about one which I want to talk about first, ask you about - Davy Tough.

Now, without David Tough you would never have heard of none of the musicians supposed to be in Chicago, because Davy Tough dared to go over to the South Side and Davy Tough - I'll explain here about Davy. Davy would go over to the South Side and go back and show the guys what he had learned from the black musicians. But they wouldn't dare do what Davy did. They'd let Davy do it. That's the reason all these people got all these great names, but they would not go where Davy went. They called him a drunken bum, Davy came from a nice family. You always caught Davy in a gutter somewhere full of that corn whiskey. You remember those stills used to blow up? He knew before the police whose still it was. He said 'Oh my God, they done blew up my whisky.'

Ah look, Davy wasted all his energy and time to try to go and tell a saxophone player, try to tell a trumpet player... try to tell anybody, this is what I heard last night and he'd sit them down and try to show them what he heard. But it was too much, as small as he was, and he had a thyroid gland condition.
He was a tiny man, wasn't he?

A tiny man, yes, and they didn't understand him to his death. Without Davy Tough you would have never heard - and I'll say it and I know that I know what I'm talking about - you never would have heard of all the peoples that have got these reputations out here that were supposed to have been so great in Chicago. But you must remember Davy was fortunate enough to be around Jimmy Bertrand. Davy Tough was fortunate enough to be around with Walter Bishop, but these other guys -
